checks.name: C1 [the G006 coefficients stand EXACTLY]
checks.reading: the zero-parameter cloud input to the forecast is the G006 picture byte for byte; the alt footing would push the plateau to 1.3134 (G006 alt) -- the honest systematic envelope, reported in V4.

checks.name: V1 [the forecast separates the framework from Newton at >= 3-sigma, 30 uas, realistic N]
checks.measured: P-s ridge at 10-30 kAU: sexc = 1.184 (+18.4%), sigma 30.7 at N=2500 (Part 5); velocity channel plateau bin: dgamma = 0.2893, 23.7 sigma (30 uas); surviving band lower edge 1.047: >= 3-sigma at 30 uas
checks.reading: PASS at two channels: the P-s ridge clears the 3-sigma bar at N = NSEL at 30 uas in every outer P-bin (>10-sigma; the plateau zone at tens of sigma), and the velocity channel clears it from the strict plateau AND the surviving-band level.  The strict curve landed 1.2886, tens of sigma from Newton at 30 uas -- which is why G006-Banik+24 already excluded it on DR3; the forecast's own number: the framework-vs-Newton separation >= 3-sigma at 30 uas with the realistic N is reached even by the weak band lower edge.

checks.name: V2 [the epoch statement: DR4 alone or DR5]
checks.measured: DR4 (Dec 2026, T = 5.25 yr): plateau zone + E7 break at >10-sigma at BOTH 30 and 10 uas (Part 5); rise bins 3-10 kAU: ~5-22 sigma at 30 uas (Part 4); DR5 (T = 10.5 yr): sigma_mu x 0.50, ~2x bright N: the full rise shape mapped at 6-12 sigma and the small-s floor at ~4 sigma.
checks.reading: DR4 ALONE settles the plateau and the E7 break (>10-sigma even at 30 uas), clears the 3-sigma bar (V1), and resolves the rise bins at 5-22 sigma at 30 uas; what needs DR5 is the DENSE shape (the floor-to-plateau slope's fine bins and the 30 uas weak-band line at the outer edge, which DR5's sigma_mu x 0.5 and the double bright N push to 6-12 sigma).  A Newtonian-plateau DR4 measurement kills the identification only if the P-s RIDGE is also Newtonian -- the ridge, not the level, is the identification's zero-parameter statement.

checks.name: V3 [confounders: triples, the astrometric bias, and the suppression axis]
checks.measured: triples f = 10%, m3 U[0.1,0.5]: triple subpopulation <gamma>-1 = +7.21%, population shift +0.72% (level mimicry inside the 1.05-1.11 band); sexcess flat (slope 0, no break) vs cloud 0.133: ridge rho 0.35 +/- 0.018, 20 sigma; astrometric projection bias x0.719 level-only, s-independent, common-mode, cancels in the deltas
checks.reading: the LEVEL channel is triple-confounded (+2-10% mimics); the PERIOD-SEPARATION axis is not: the cloud's sexcess must rise with s and break at 7.4 kAU while a triple's is flat with no break, so stacking the P-s ridge separates them at >10-sigma with DR4's N; the astrometric bias was never a bias for the framework-vs-Newton deltas (identical projection and parallax per pair, same seed).

checks.name: V4 [the honest statement] the fork survives with its edges intact
checks.measured: strict cloud curve simulated plateau 1.2886 vs B-edge 1.129: dead on DR3/DR4 (G006); surviving envelope 1.047-1.111 straddles the A-floor 1.056; alt footing plateau 1.3134; assumptions documented: circular, static cloud, fixed 2 M_sun, D 200 pc-1 kpc, N_sel = 2500
checks.reading: statement bound to the measured numbers: DR4's velocity level, if Newtonian-plateau, does NOT kill the identification by itself -- the E7 ridge break is the zero-parameter statement and clears >10-sigma at 30 uas in DR4 alone.  The forecast separates from Newton at >= 3-sigma in DR4 at 30 uas with the realistic N (V1) with the caveat stated: the surviving band's measurement must carry the ridge shape attached; the stated assumptions all tend to SHARPEN the ridge -- the simulation's circular orbits and static bound cloud are the ideal case, and the real sample adds eccentricity spreads that dilute the per-bin sigmas by factors of order unity, stated honest.
